title: The Peace of Qurṭuba: Castile, its armies and its spirit broken by the plague, begs a separate peace of Granada alone, and to the court's surprise accepts its sharp demands

terms: Granada takes 23 locations, from Qurṭuba and Ishbīliyya to Jayyān, Úbeda, Baeza and Écija
the Ṭāʾifa of Mursiyya takes the Murcia area, eleven more locations
Castile pays war reparations to Granada
Castile annuls all treaties with Aragon
Granada returns to the name of Castile's tributary

source: Trent's account and screenshot; checkpoint 1349-01-27 (saves before and after the peace)

title: Granada is again Castile's tributary, though only in name: it holds 53 of the 72 locations of the Strait's three areas, against 19 before the war
The realm doubles: 754,000 souls in 41 locations, and nearly half of them Castilian Christians; the Ṭāʾifa of Mursiyya now holds Mursiyya, Qarṭājanna, Lawraqa and the whole Murcia area
Plague and war have left the realm unsettled: stability stands below zero, at −1.6

With the gold of the peace, Yūsuf lays the foundations of a new wing of al-Ḥamrāʾ on the Sabīka hill, its vaults in muqarnas and its walls cut with verse, to tell Castile and Morocco alike that the house of Naṣr means to stay

data.strait: each completed tier adds 0.05 sovereignty a month (game files)

source: Trent's account and screenshots (under construction by 1 June 1349; the day the works began isn't given)

title: An Embassy to al-Qāhira: Yūsuf sends an envoy across the sea to Sultan Jamāl al-Dīn of Egypt, keeper of the holy cities, at the cost of a quarter of a year's income

data.choice: Send an envoy across the sea to Al-Qāhira.
data.followUp: A Plea from the West (Egypt's answer pending)

title: The estates read off the panel after the peace: the crown at 27%, the nobility down to 31%, and the Dhimmī, swollen by the Christians of the new lands, at 21%

data.note: screen values; the first full reading since 11 August 1340

source: Trent's screenshot of the estates panel, 1 June 1349

title: In the conquered lands Castilian patriots are gathering in rebellion, while the dīwān works to integrate Jayyān and Ishbīliyya and the plague goes on taking the people
The Mamlūks answer as brothers in faith: an alliance with Granada, Mamlūk horse and foot sent to Gharnāṭa, and yearly gold and men
Sovereignty rises above 50 again, to 53.4, for the first time since August 1346; influence stands at +5.5
With the Mamlūk alliance stretching the court's diplomacy far beyond its means (10.65 of 6.07), Yūsuf lets the alliance with Tunis lapse; the Moroccan alliance stands for now

data.overLimitPenalty: half the overage: crown power −37.6% falls to about −18.8%

source: Trent's account and screenshot of the diplomatic capacity (the exact day isn't given; just after 4 June 1349)

title: The Great Dying: the pestilence has now killed 210,000 of the realm's people, against 9,000 a year before, and lies over 17 locations, worst across the newly won lands of Andalusia; across the known world nearly 44 million are dead
source: Trent's screenshot of the Black Death panel
